If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have  

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 5\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{3} \\ 0 \\ 5{x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=2 \\ {x}_{2}=3 \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3}=-1\end{aligned}
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 5 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 5 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=2 \\ {x}_{2}=3 \\ {x}_{3}=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-3$ and from the second equation we get ${x}_{2}=3.$ Substituting these into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}-3+2(-3)=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=11.
$$

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=11$, ${x}_{2}=3$, and ${x}_{3}=-3,$ which means 

$$
11{a}_{1}+3{a}_{2}-3{a}_{3}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=11+3-3=11.
$$

M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 2 & 0 & -4\end{bmatrix}
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 2 & 0 & -4\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 5\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0.2 & 0.8 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :=-{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0.2 & 0.8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-3 \\ {x}_{2}+\,0.2{x}_{3} &=0.8 \\ {x}_{3} &=-1.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-1.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get 

$$
{x}_{2}+0.2(-1)=0.8\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=1.
$$

   

Finally,  substituting ${x}_{2}=1$ into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}-(1)=-3\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-2.
$$

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-2$, ${x}_{2}=1$, and ${x}_{3}=-1,$ which means  

$$
-2{a}_{1}+{a}_{2}-{a}_{3}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-2+1-1=-2.
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ 2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ {x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{3} \\ -2{x}_{3} \\ 0\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2}-2{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{3} &=8 \\ {x}_{2}-2{x}_{3} &=-6 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -14\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & -20\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{4}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{3} &=8 \\ {x}_{2}-2{x}_{3} &=-6 \\ {x}_{3} &=5.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=5.$ Substituting this value in the second and first equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & {x}_{2}-2(5)=-6\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=4 \\  & {x}_{1}+5=8\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=3$, ${x}_{2}=4$, and ${x}_{3}=5,$ which means 

$$
3{a}_{1}+4{a}_{2}+5{a}_{3}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=3+4+5=12.
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-5 \\ -8 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 9 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-5 \\ -8 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 9 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-5{x}_{2} \\ -8{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 9 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} \\ -{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 9 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} &=1 \\ 2{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} &=9 \\ -{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -8 & 2 & 9 \\ -1 & 5 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -8 & 2 & 9 \\ -1 & 5 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & 7 \\ -1 & 5 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} &=1 \\ 2{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3} &=7 \\ 0 &=2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

However, the final equation $0=2$  gives a false statement. So the system has no solution.

:step/content.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ 1 \\ -4\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
:step/content.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ 1 \\ -4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ 1 \\ -4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ 1 \\ -4\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-3 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=1 \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=-4\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $2$ and adding the resulting equations, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =-5,\end{aligned}
$$

which we substitute into the second equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=1 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3(-5) & =1 \\ -2{x}_{1} & =-14 \\ {x}_{1} & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=7$ and ${x}_{2}=-5$ into the third equation and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=-4 \\ 3(7)+5(-5) & =-4 \\ -4 & =-4,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=7$ and ${x}_{2}=-5,$ which means

$$
7{a}_{1}-5{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=7+(-5)=2.
$$

:step/content.:question/problem:
Find the value of ${x}_{1}-{x}_{2}$ given that  $4a+3x=b$ and

$$
a=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,x=\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}18 \\ -15 \\ -9\end{bmatrix}.
$$
:step/content.:question/worked-solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4a+3x & =b \\ 3x & =b-4a \\ x & =\frac{1}{3}(b-4a) \\ x & =\frac{1}{3}(\begin{bmatrix}18 \\ -15 \\ -9\end{bmatrix}-4\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}) \\ x & =\frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}6 \\ -27 \\ -21\end{bmatrix} \\ x & =\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -9 \\ -7\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=2-(-9)=11.$

:step/content.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -11 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -18 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
:step/content.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -11 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -18 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{3} \\ -11{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -18 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} \\ -2{x}_{2}-11{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -18 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=5 \\ -2{x}_{2}-11{x}_{3} &=-18 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -18 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -18 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -18 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -18\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & -15 & -30\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{15}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=5 \\ {x}_{2}-2{x}_{3} &=-6 \\ {x}_{3} &=2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

 

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=2.$ Substituting this value into  the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}-2(2)=-6\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-2.
$$

 

Finally, by substituting ${x}_{2}=-2$ and ${x}_{3}=2$ into the first equation, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} & =5 \\ {x}_{1}+(-2)+3(2) & =5 \\ {x}_{1}+4 & =5 \\ {x}_{1} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=1$, ${x}_{2}=-2$, and ${x}_{3}=2,$ which means 

$$
{a}_{1}-2{a}_{2}+2{a}_{3}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=1+(-2)+2=1.
$$

:step/content.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
:step/content.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then   we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -3\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -{x}_{3} \\ -3{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-2 \\ -{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} &=5 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3} &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & 5 \\ 1 & -1 & -3 & 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & 5 \\ 1 & -1 & -3 & 1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 & 3\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :=(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 & 3\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -12\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-2 \\ {x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=-5 \\ 0 &=-12.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

However, the final equation $0=-12$  gives a false statement. So the system has no solution.

:step/content.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 3 \\ -3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ 8 \\ -14\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
:step/content.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 3 \\ -3\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ 8 \\ -14\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-2{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ 8 \\ -14\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ 8 \\ -14\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} &=-11 \\ 4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=8 \\ 2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-14\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the second and the third equations we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}6{x}_{1} & =-6 \\ {x}_{1} & =-1,\end{aligned}
$$

which we substitute into the second equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} & =8 \\ 4(-1)+3{x}_{2} & =8 \\ 3{x}_{2} & =12 \\ {x}_{2} & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=4$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} & =-11 \\ 3(-1)-2(4) & =-11 \\ -11 & =-11,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=4,$ which means

$$
-{a}_{1}+4{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-1+4=3.
$$

![](images/c7/c715fd50dbcc9251cd7c01e033ba59be2af244d57ec02b707aa7cd8764e58d58.svg)
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the $s$ term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{a}_{1}+s{a}_{2} & =b \\ 3\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+s\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}13 \\ 6 \\ -5\end{bmatrix} \\ s\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}13 \\ 6 \\ -5\end{bmatrix}-3\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ s\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}16 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the final equation above, we can tell that $s=4.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:

$$

$$

Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the $k$ term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{a}_{1}+k{a}_{2} & =0 \\ 3\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}+k\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ k\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}-3\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ k\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ -12\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the first components, we get 

$$

$$

But then

$$
\begin{aligned}-2\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ -4\end{bmatrix}\ne \begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ -12\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, there is no $k$ such that $3{a}_{1}+k{a}_{2}=0.$

If $x_1 \mathbf{c}_1 + x_2\mathbf{c}_2  = \mathbf d,$ then what is $x_1+x_2?$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
If $x_1 \mathbf{c}_1 + x_2\mathbf{c}_2  = \mathbf d,$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -5 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -5 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=5 \\ -{x}_{1} &=-5 \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the second equation, we obtain $x_1=5,$ which we substitute into the first equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & =5 \\ 4(5)+{x}_{2} & =5 \\ {x}_{2} & =-15.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $x_1=5$ and $x_2=-15$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & =0 \\ 3(5)+(-15) & =0 \\ 0 & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is $x_1=5$ and $x_2=-15,$ which means

$$
5 \mathbf{c_1}-15 \mathbf{c_2} = \mathbf{d}.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_1+x_2=5-15=-10.
$$

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=5 \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=3 \\ {x}_{2} &=2\end{aligned}\right.

$$

$$

$$

\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ 9 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}4{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ 9 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ 9 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=7 \\ -2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=9 \\ 3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=4\end{aligned}\right.
$$

$$

$$

Now,  we substitute ${x}_{1}=3$ into the third equation to get 

$$

$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=5$ into the second equation to get

$$

$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=5,$ which means

$$

Consequently, 

$$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Solving for Two Coefficients in a Linear Combination

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

![](images/16/1687c0a08fedfd90a26481007bb9bf56263edf67574fd690662064ef0341c86c.svg)

If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 + x_3\mathbf{a}_3 = \mathbf b,$ then what is $x_1+x_2+x_3?$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Since $\mathbf{b}$ is a linear combination of vectors $\mathbf{a_1}, \,\mathbf{a_2}$ and $\mathbf{a_3}$ with coefficients $x_1,\, x_2$ and $x_3,$ respectively, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3} & =b \\ {x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ {x}_{1} \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{2} \\ 0 \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3} \\ 3{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{3} \\ -{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=1 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{3} &=1 \\ -{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=7\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

![](images/9b/9bf913744317fab321cf9f2e01da732853a52a4fd7948c65da596ae4706f6dce.svg)

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 & 7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 & 7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 8\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{3} &=1 \\ {x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=1 \\ {x}_{3} &=2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3 = 2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
x_2+(2) = 1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x_2 = -1,
$$

and substituting $x_3=2$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x_1+2(2) = 1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1 = -3.
$$

So the solution of the system is $x_1=-3, x_2=-1, x_3=2,$ which means

$$
-3 \mathbf{a_1}- \mathbf{a_2} +2 \mathbf{a_3}= \mathbf{b}.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_1+x_2+x_3=-3-1+2=-2.
$$

$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=2 \\ {x}_{2}=3 \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3}=-1\end{aligned}
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 5 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 5 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=2 \\ {x}_{2}=3 \\ {x}_{3}=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-3$ and from the second equation we get ${x}_{2}=3.$ Substituting these into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}-3+2(-3)=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=11.

$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=11+3-3=11.
$$

$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -5 \\ -3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -21 \\ -12\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ 14 \\ 9\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 8 \\ -7\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ -5{x}_{1} \\ -3{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}4{x}_{2} \\ -21{x}_{2} \\ -12{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-3{x}_{3} \\ 14{x}_{3} \\ 9{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 8 \\ -7\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3} \\ -5{x}_{1}-21{x}_{2}+14{x}_{3} \\ -3{x}_{1}-12{x}_{2}+9{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 8 \\ -7\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3} &=2 \\ -5{x}_{1}-21{x}_{2}+14{x}_{3} &=8 \\ -3{x}_{1}-12{x}_{2}+9{x}_{3} &=-7\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 4 & -3 & 2 \\ -5 & -21 & 14 & 8 \\ -3 & -12 & 9 & -7\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 4 & -3 & 2 \\ -5 & -21 & 14 & 8 \\ -3 & -12 & 9 & -7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 4 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & 18 \\ -3 & -12 & 9 & -7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 4 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & 18 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3} &=2 \\ -{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} &=18 \\ 0 &=-1.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

However, the final equation $0=-1$  gives a false statement. So the system has no solution.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-5 \\ -10 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{2} \\ 0 \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{3} \\ 5{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-5 \\ -10 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} \\ 5{x}_{3} \\ 3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-5 \\ -10 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} &=-5 \\ 5{x}_{3} &=-10 \\ 3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -10 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -10 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -10 \\ 0 & 2 & -5 & 16\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 2 & -5 & 16 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -10\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2.5 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -10\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2.5 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} &=-5 \\ {x}_{2}-2.5\,{x}_{3} &=8 \\ {x}_{3} &=-2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-2.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get 

$$
{x}_{2}-2.5(-2)=8\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=8-5=3.
$$

Finally,  substituting ${x}_{2}=3$ and ${x}_{3}=-2$  into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}-(3)+2(-2)=-5\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2.
$$

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=2$, ${x}_{2}=3$, and ${x}_{3}=-2,$ which means 

$$
2{a}_{1}+3{a}_{2}-2{a}_{3}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=2+3-2=3.
$$

$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=-1 \\ 3{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=-9 \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -9 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -9 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -9 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=-1 \\ {x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=-3 \\ {x}_{3} &=-1.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

 

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-1.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}+(-1)=-3\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-2.

Finally, by substituting ${x}_{2}=-2,{x}_{3}=-1$ into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} & =-1 \\ {x}_{1}+(-2)+3(-1) & =-1 \\ {x}_{1}-5 & =-1 \\ {x}_{1} & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=4$, ${x}_{2}=-2$, and ${x}_{3}=-1,$ which means 

$$
4{a}_{1}-2{a}_{2}-{a}_{3}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$

$$

$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=5 \\ -2{x}_{2}-11{x}_{3} &=-18 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=-1\end{aligned}\right.

$$

$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -18 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -18 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -18\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & -15 & -30\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{15}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}

$$

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-3 \\ 5{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=4 \\ 3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-4\end{aligned}\right.

$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-5 \\ -8 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 9 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-5{x}_{2} \\ -8{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 9 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} \\ -{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 9 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} &=1 \\ 2{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} &=9 \\ -{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -8 & 2 & 9 \\ -1 & 5 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -8 & 2 & 9 \\ -1 & 5 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & 7 \\ -1 & 5 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} &=1 \\ 2{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3} &=7 \\ 0 &=2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

However, the final equation $0=2$  gives a false statement. So the system has no solution.

:step/content.:tutorial/content:
Consider a vector $\mathbf{u}$ which is given in terms of the vectors $\mathbf{v_1}$ and $\mathbf{v_2}$ as follows:

$$
{\color{red}3}{\color{blue}\mathbf{v_1}}+({\color{red}-2}){\color{blue}\mathbf{v_2}} = \mathbf{u}
$$

Here, we say that $\mathbf{u}$ is a **linear combination** of the vectors ${\color{blue}\mathbf{v_1}}$ and ${\color{blue}\mathbf{v_2}}$ with coefficients ${\color{red}3}$ and ${\color{red}-2}$ respectively. 

In general, a linear combination of $n$ vectors $\mathbf{v_1},\mathbf{v_2},\dots,\mathbf{v_n}$ is the *weighted sum*

$$
{\color{red}x_1}\mathbf{\color{blue}v_1}+{\color{red}x_2}\mathbf{\color{blue}v_2}+\cdots + {\color{red}x_n}\mathbf{\color{blue}v_n} = \mathbf{u},
$$

where ${\color{red}x_1},{\color{red}x_2},\dots,{\color{red}x_n}\in\mathbb{R}.$ We say that $\mathbf{u}$ is a linear combination of the vectors $\mathbf{\color{blue}v_1},\mathbf{\color{blue}v_2},\dots,\mathbf{\color{blue}v_n}$ with coefficients (or *weights*) ${\color{red}x_1},{\color{red}x_2},\dots,{\color{red}x_n},$ respectively.

For instance, 
![](images/ff/ff71636b9b5a34fec4de37b5e924c1c6bc3765c1ee823b325f5b0e01c0dc472a.svg)
is the linear combination of vectors $\mathbf{\color{blue}v_1},\mathbf{\color{blue}v_2},\mathbf{\color{blue}v_3}$ with coefficients ${\color{red}2}, {\color{red}0}, {\color{red}\dfrac{1}{2}},$ respectively.

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

![](images/0b/0b7919416954fe536a93f681fb3c56cac8dddff67e389ef233fdb242390dfb91.svg)

If $x_1 \mathbf{c}_1 + x_2\mathbf{c}_2  = \mathbf d,$ then what is $x_1+x_2?$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
If $x_1 \mathbf{c}_1 + x_2\mathbf{c}_2  = \mathbf d,$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -5 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -5 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=5 \\ -{x}_{1} &=-5 \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the second equation, we obtain $x_1=5,$ which we substitute into the first equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & =5 \\ 4(5)+{x}_{2} & =5 \\ {x}_{2} & =-15.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $x_1=5$ and $x_2=-15$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & =0 \\ 3(5)+(-15) & =0 \\ 0 & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is $x_1=5$ and $x_2=-15,$ which means

$$
5 \mathbf{c_1}-15 \mathbf{c_2} = \mathbf{d}.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_1+x_2=5-15=-10.
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=5 \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=3 \\ {x}_{2} &=2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation we get ${x}_{2}=2$, which we substitute into the second equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & =3 \\ -{x}_{1}+2 & =3 \\ {x}_{1} & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=2$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} & =5 \\ -(-1)+2(2) & =5 \\ 5 & =5,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=2,$ which means

$$
-{a}_{1}+2{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-1+2=1.
$$

$$

 

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$

:step/content.:knowledge-point/title: Solving for Two Coefficients in a Linear Combination

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

![](images/16/1687c0a08fedfd90a26481007bb9bf56263edf67574fd690662064ef0341c86c.svg)

If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 + x_3\mathbf{a}_3 = \mathbf b,$ then what is $x_1+x_2+x_3?$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Since $\mathbf{b}$ is a linear combination of vectors $\mathbf{a_1}, \,\mathbf{a_2}$ and $\mathbf{a_3}$ with coefficients $x_1,\, x_2$ and $x_3,$ respectively, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3} & =b \\ {x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ {x}_{1} \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{2} \\ 0 \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3} \\ 3{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{3} \\ -{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=1 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{3} &=1 \\ -{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=7\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

![](images/9b/9bf913744317fab321cf9f2e01da732853a52a4fd7948c65da596ae4706f6dce.svg)

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 & 7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 & 7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 8\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{3} &=1 \\ {x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=1 \\ {x}_{3} &=2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3 = 2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
x_2+(2) = 1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x_2 = -1,
$$

and substituting $x_3=2$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x_1+2(2) = 1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1 = -3.
$$

So the solution of the system is $x_1=-3, x_2=-1, x_3=2,$ which means

$$
-3 \mathbf{a_1}- \mathbf{a_2} +2 \mathbf{a_3}= \mathbf{b}.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_1+x_2+x_3=-3-1+2=-2.
$$

$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=2 \\ {x}_{2}=3 \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3}=-1\end{aligned}
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 5 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 5 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=2 \\ {x}_{2}=3 \\ {x}_{3}=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-3$ and from the second equation we get ${x}_{2}=3.$ Substituting these into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}-3+2(-3)=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=11.

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=11$, ${x}_{2}=3$, and ${x}_{3}=-3,$ which means 

$$
11{a}_{1}+3{a}_{2}-3{a}_{3}=b.

Consequently, 

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & -8 & 5 & 1 \\ -2 & 6 & -3 & 2\end{bmatrix}
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$

\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{3} &=8 \\ {x}_{2}-2{x}_{3} &=-6 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -14\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & -20\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{4}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{3} &=8 \\ {x}_{2}-2{x}_{3} &=-6 \\ {x}_{3} &=5.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=5.$ Substituting this value in the second and first equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & {x}_{2}-2(5)=-6\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=4 \\  & {x}_{1}+5=8\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=3$, ${x}_{2}=4$, and ${x}_{3}=5,$ which means 

$$
3{a}_{1}+4{a}_{2}+5{a}_{3}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=3+4+5=12.
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-5 \\ -8 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 9 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-5 \\ -8 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 9 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-5{x}_{2} \\ -8{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 9 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} \\ -{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 9 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} &=1 \\ 2{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} &=9 \\ -{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -8 & 2 & 9 \\ -1 & 5 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -8 & 2 & 9 \\ -1 & 5 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & 7 \\ -1 & 5 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} &=1 \\ 2{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3} &=7 \\ 0 &=2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

However, the final equation $0=2$  gives a false statement. So the system has no solution.

Consider a vector $\mathbf{u}$ which is given in terms of the vectors $\mathbf{v_1}$ and $\mathbf{v_2}$ as follows:

$$
{\color{red}3}{\color{blue}\mathbf{v_1}}+({\color{red}-2}){\color{blue}\mathbf{v_2}} = \mathbf{u}
$$

Here, we say that $\mathbf{u}$ is a **linear combination** of the vectors ${\color{blue}\mathbf{v_1}}$ and ${\color{blue}\mathbf{v_2}}$ with coefficients ${\color{red}3}$ and ${\color{red}-2}$ respectively. 

In general, a linear combination of $n$ vectors $\mathbf{v_1},\mathbf{v_2},\dots,\mathbf{v_n}$ is the *weighted sum*

$$
{\color{red}x_1}\mathbf{\color{blue}v_1}+{\color{red}x_2}\mathbf{\color{blue}v_2}+\cdots + {\color{red}x_n}\mathbf{\color{blue}v_n} = \mathbf{u},
$$

where ${\color{red}x_1},{\color{red}x_2},\dots,{\color{red}x_n}\in\mathbb{R}.$ We say that $\mathbf{u}$ is a linear combination of the vectors $\mathbf{\color{blue}v_1},\mathbf{\color{blue}v_2},\dots,\mathbf{\color{blue}v_n}$ with coefficients (or *weights*) ${\color{red}x_1},{\color{red}x_2},\dots,{\color{red}x_n},$ respectively.

Find $s,$ if $3\mathbf{a_1}+s\mathbf{a_2} = \mathbf{b}$ and
![](images/c7/c715fd50dbcc9251cd7c01e033ba59be2af244d57ec02b707aa7cd8764e58d58.svg)
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the $s$ term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{a}_{1}+s{a}_{2} & =b \\ 3\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+s\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}13 \\ 6 \\ -5\end{bmatrix} \\ s\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}13 \\ 6 \\ -5\end{bmatrix}-3\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ s\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}16 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the final equation above, we can tell that $s=4.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Find $k$, if $3{a}_{1}+k{a}_{2}=0$ and 

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}.
$$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the $k$ term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{a}_{1}+k{a}_{2} & =0 \\ 3\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}+k\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ k\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}-3\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ k\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ -12\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the first components, we get 

$$
3k=-6\,⟹\,k=-2.
$$

But then

$$
\begin{aligned}-2\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ -4\end{bmatrix}\ne \begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ -12\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, there is no $k$ such that $3{a}_{1}+k{a}_{2}=0.$

$$

$$

$$

:step/content.:tutorial/content:
Suppose that we want to solve, *without* using graphs, the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y &=4 \\ x-2 &=y\,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

In order to solve the system without a graph, we will need to combine the equations into a single equation that can be solved using algebraic manipulation.

One way to combine the equations is called the **substitution method.** To use the substitution method, we substitute for one variable in terms of the other.

For instance, notice that we can make $y$ the subject of the second equation:

$$
\color{red}y=x - 2
$$

Substituting this expression for $y$ into the first equation, we get an equation that we can solve for $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}x+y & =4 \\ x+(x-2) & =4 \\ 2x-2 & =4 \\ 2x & =6 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution must have $x=3.$ But we also need to figure out what $y$ is. We can do this by substituting $x=3$ back into the second equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =x-2 \\ y & =3-2 \\ y & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x = 3$ and $y = 1$, which can be written as $\left(3, 1\right).$

**Note:** Whenever we isolate the variable in one equation, we have to substitute it into the *other* equation. We cannot substitute a variable into the same equation it came from, because this will not give us any more information about the variable.

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y &=4 \\ x+2y &=16\end{aligned}\right.
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. It doesn't matter which equation we pick first, so we choose the easiest one. In this case, the first equation looks like the easiest.

Using the first equation, we can isolate $x$ by adding $y$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-y & =4 \\ x & =4+y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we replace $x$ with $4+y$ in the second equation and solve for $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\eqalign{
	x+2y &=16 \
	(4+y) + 2y &=16\
	4+3y &=16\
	3y &=12\
	y &=4
}
$$

If we now substitute $y=4$ into $x=4+y$, then we can find the value of $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\eqalign{
	x &= 4 + y \
	   &= 4 + (4) \
	   &=8
}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x = 8$ and $y = 4$, which can be written as $(8, 4).$

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2u+9v-6 &=0 \\ 2u+6v-8 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Sometimes, it's handy to assign a number to each equation in a system, so that we can refer to them more easily:
![](images/77/77459b19bb1fd1f28e05e6f613e4e49af34595eae33eeeca584d65a289f7ea2c.svg)

We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. Using equation $\color{blue}(2)$, we can solve for $u$ as follows:

$$
\eqalign{
	2u+6v-8 &= 0 \
2u+6v &= 8 \
2u &= 8 - 6v \
u &= \dfrac{8-6v}{2} \
u &= 4 - 3v
}
$$

Then, we substitute $u=4-3v$ into equation $\color{red}(1)$ and solve for $v\mathbin{:}$

$$
\eqalign{
	2u+9v-6 &= 0 \
	2(4-3v)+9v-6 &= 0 \
	8-6v+9v-6 &= 0 \
2+3v &= 0 \
3v &= -2 \
v &= -\dfrac{2}{3}
}
$$

If we now substitute $v=-\dfrac{2}{3}$ into equation $\color{red}(1)$, then we can find the value of $u\mathbin{:}$

$$
\eqalign{
	2u+9v-6 &= 0 \
	2u+9\left(-\dfrac{2}{3}\right) -6 &= 0 \
	2u-6-6 &= 0 \
	2u-12 &= 0 \
	2u &= 12 \
	u &= 6
}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $u=6$ and $v=-\dfrac{2}{3}$, which can be written as $\left(6,-\dfrac{2}{3}\right).$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}d-50t=190 \\ d=190+50t\end{aligned}
$$

So, we replace $d$ with $190+50t$ in the first equation and solve for $t:$

$$

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2u+9v-6 &=0 \\ 2u+6v-8 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Sometimes, it's handy to assign a number to each equation in a system, so that we can refer to them more easily:
![](images/77/77459b19bb1fd1f28e05e6f613e4e49af34595eae33eeeca584d65a289f7ea2c.svg)

We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. Using equation $\color{blue}(2)$, we can solve for $u$ as follows:

$$
\eqalign{
	2u+6v-8 &= 0 \
2u+6v &= 8 \
2u &= 8 - 6v \
u &= \dfrac{8-6v}{2} \
u &= 4 - 3v
}
$$

Then, we substitute $u=4-3v$ into equation $\color{red}(1)$ and solve for $v\mathbin{:}$

$$
\eqalign{
	2u+9v-6 &= 0 \
	2(4-3v)+9v-6 &= 0 \
	8-6v+9v-6 &= 0 \
2+3v &= 0 \
3v &= -2 \
v &= -\dfrac{2}{3}
}
$$

If we now substitute $v=-\dfrac{2}{3}$ into equation $\color{red}(1)$, then we can find the value of $u\mathbin{:}$

$$
\eqalign{
	2u+9v-6 &= 0 \
	2u+9\left(-\dfrac{2}{3}\right) -6 &= 0 \
	2u-6-6 &= 0 \
	2u-12 &= 0 \
	2u &= 12 \
	u &= 6
}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $u=6$ and $v=-\dfrac{2}{3}$, which can be written as $\left(6,-\dfrac{2}{3}\right).$

$$

$$

$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=-1 \\ 3{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=-9 \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -9 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -9 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -9 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=-1 \\ {x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=-3 \\ {x}_{3} &=-1.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

 

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-1.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}+(-1)=-3\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-2.
$$

Finally, by substituting ${x}_{2}=-2,{x}_{3}=-1$ into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} & =-1 \\ {x}_{1}+(-2)+3(-1) & =-1 \\ {x}_{1}-5 & =-1 \\ {x}_{1} & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=4$, ${x}_{2}=-2$, and ${x}_{3}=-1,$ which means 

$$

$$

Consequently, 

$$

$$

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-3 \\ 5{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=4 \\ 3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-4\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$

{x}_{1}-(1)=-3\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-2.

:step/content.:knowledge-point/title: Solving for Three Coefficients in a Linear Combination

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

![](images/16/1687c0a08fedfd90a26481007bb9bf56263edf67574fd690662064ef0341c86c.svg)

If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 + x_3\mathbf{a}_3 = \mathbf b,$ then what is $x_1+x_2+x_3?$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Since $\mathbf{b}$ is a linear combination of vectors $\mathbf{a_1}, \,\mathbf{a_2}$ and $\mathbf{a_3}$ with coefficients $x_1,\, x_2$ and $x_3,$ respectively, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3} & =b \\ {x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ {x}_{1} \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{2} \\ 0 \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3} \\ 3{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{3} \\ -{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=1 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{3} &=1 \\ -{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=7\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

![](images/9b/9bf913744317fab321cf9f2e01da732853a52a4fd7948c65da596ae4706f6dce.svg)

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 & 7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 & 7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 8\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{3} &=1 \\ {x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=1 \\ {x}_{3} &=2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3 = 2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
x_2+(2) = 1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x_2 = -1,
$$

and substituting $x_3=2$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x_1+2(2) = 1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1 = -3.
$$

So the solution of the system is $x_1=-3, x_2=-1, x_3=2,$ which means

$$
-3 \mathbf{a_1}- \mathbf{a_2} +2 \mathbf{a_3}= \mathbf{b}.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_1+x_2+x_3=-3-1+2=-2.
$$

$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 5 \\ 6\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 2 \\ 9\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ -6 \\ 7\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2} \\ 6{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3} \\ 9{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ -6 \\ 7\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} \\ 3{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}+9{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ -6 \\ 7\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=-2 \\ 2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} &=-6 \\ 3{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}+9{x}_{3} &=7\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 5 & 2 & -6 \\ 3 & 6 & 9 & 7\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 5 & 2 & -6 \\ 3 & 6 & 9 & 7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -2 \\ 3 & 6 & 9 & 7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 13\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=-2 \\ {x}_{2}-4{x}_{3} &=-2 \\ 0 &=13.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

However, the final equation $0=13$  gives a false statement. So the system has no solution.

$$

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} &=2 \\ 3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3} &=1 \\ -2{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3} &=2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & -8 & 5 & 1 \\ -2 & 6 & -3 & 2\end{bmatrix}
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & -8 & 5 & 1 \\ -2 & 6 & -3 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -5 \\ -2 & 6 & -3 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 6\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}

$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-5 \\ -10 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{2} \\ 0 \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{3} \\ 5{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-5 \\ -10 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} \\ 5{x}_{3} \\ 3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-5 \\ -10 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} &=-5 \\ 5{x}_{3} &=-10 \\ 3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -10 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -10 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -10 \\ 0 & 2 & -5 & 16\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 2 & -5 & 16 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -10\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2.5 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -10\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2.5 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} &=-5 \\ {x}_{2}-2.5\,{x}_{3} &=8 \\ {x}_{3} &=-2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

$$
{x}_{2}-2.5(-2)=8\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=8-5=3.

$$
{x}_{1}-(3)+2(-2)=-5\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2.

$$
2{a}_{1}+3{a}_{2}-2{a}_{3}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=2+3-2=3.
$$

$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=-1 \\ 3{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=-9 \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -9 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -9 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & -9 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The system is now 

$$

$$

 

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-1.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -11 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -18 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{3} \\ -11{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -18 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} \\ -2{x}_{2}-11{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -18 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=5 \\ -2{x}_{2}-11{x}_{3} &=-18 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -18 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -18 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -18 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -18\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & -15 & -30\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{15}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=5 \\ {x}_{2}-2{x}_{3} &=-6 \\ {x}_{3} &=2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

 

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=2.$ Substituting this value into  the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}-2(2)=-6\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-2.

Finally, by substituting ${x}_{2}=-2$ and ${x}_{3}=2$ into the first equation, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} & =5 \\ {x}_{1}+(-2)+3(2) & =5 \\ {x}_{1}+4 & =5 \\ {x}_{1} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=1$, ${x}_{2}=-2$, and ${x}_{3}=2,$ which means 

$$
{a}_{1}-2{a}_{2}+2{a}_{3}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=1+(-2)+2=1.
$$

If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 + x_3\mathbf{a}_3 = \mathbf b,$ then what is $x_1+x_2+x_3?$
17592186119669.:question/worked-solution:
Since $\mathbf{b}$ is a linear combination of vectors $\mathbf{a_1}, \,\mathbf{a_2}$ and $\mathbf{a_3}$ with coefficients $x_1,\, x_2$ and $x_3,$ respectively, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3} & =b \\ {x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ {x}_{1} \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{2} \\ 0 \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3} \\ 3{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{3} \\ -{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=1 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{3} &=1 \\ -{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=7\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

![](images/9b/9bf913744317fab321cf9f2e01da732853a52a4fd7948c65da596ae4706f6dce.svg)

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 & 7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 & 7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 8\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{3} &=1 \\ {x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=1 \\ {x}_{3} &=2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3 = 2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
x_2+(2) = 1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x_2 = -1,
$$

and substituting $x_3=2$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x_1+2(2) = 1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1 = -3.
$$

So the solution of the system is $x_1=-3, x_2=-1, x_3=2,$ which means

$$
-3 \mathbf{a_1}- \mathbf{a_2} +2 \mathbf{a_3}= \mathbf{b}.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_1+x_2+x_3=-3-1+2=-2.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 3 \\ -3\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ 8 \\ -14\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-2{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ 8 \\ -14\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ 8 \\ -14\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} &=-11 \\ 4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=8 \\ 2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-14\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the second and the third equations we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}6{x}_{1} & =-6 \\ {x}_{1} & =-1,\end{aligned}
$$

which we substitute into the second equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} & =8 \\ 4(-1)+3{x}_{2} & =8 \\ 3{x}_{2} & =12 \\ {x}_{2} & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=4$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} & =-11 \\ 3(-1)-2(4) & =-11 \\ -11 & =-11,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=4,$ which means

$$
-{a}_{1}+4{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-1+4=3.
$$

:step/content.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -11 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -18 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
:step/content.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -11 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -18 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{3} \\ -11{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -18 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} \\ -2{x}_{2}-11{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -18 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=5 \\ -2{x}_{2}-11{x}_{3} &=-18 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -18 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -18 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -18 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -18\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & -15 & -30\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{15}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=5 \\ {x}_{2}-2{x}_{3} &=-6 \\ {x}_{3} &=2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

 

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=2.$ Substituting this value into  the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}-2(2)=-6\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-2.
$$

 

Finally, by substituting ${x}_{2}=-2$ and ${x}_{3}=2$ into the first equation, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} & =5 \\ {x}_{1}+(-2)+3(2) & =5 \\ {x}_{1}+4 & =5 \\ {x}_{1} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=1$, ${x}_{2}=-2$, and ${x}_{3}=2,$ which means 

$$
{a}_{1}-2{a}_{2}+2{a}_{3}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=1+(-2)+2=1.
$$

:step/content.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
:step/content.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then   we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -3\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -{x}_{3} \\ -3{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-2 \\ -{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} &=5 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3} &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & 5 \\ 1 & -1 & -3 & 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & 5 \\ 1 & -1 & -3 & 1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 & 3\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :=(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 & 3\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -12\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-2 \\ {x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=-5 \\ 0 &=-12.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

However, the final equation $0=-12$  gives a false statement. So the system has no solution.

:step/content.:tutorial/content:
We can use matrices to solve systems of linear equations. To do this, we need to set up the **augmented matrix** for the system.

As an example, let's consider the system of equations below.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{\color{red}2}x+{\color{red}5}y &={\color{blue}-1} \\ {\color{red}-3}x+{\color{red}7}y &={\color{blue}1}\end{aligned}\right.
$$

First, we find the **coefficient matrix**, which consists of the coefficients of the variables:

$$
\begin{matrix}{\color{red}2} & {\color{red}5} \\ {\color{red}-3} & {\color{red}7}\end{matrix}
$$

Then, we create the **augmented matrix**. This is the coefficient matrix augmented with the column that represents the right-hand sides of the equations:

$$
\begin{array}{cc|c}{\color{red}2} & {\color{red}5} & {\color{blue}-1} \\ {\color{red}-3} & {\color{red}7} & {\color{blue}1}\end{array}
$$

In the future, we will learn how to use coefficient and augmented matrices to solve systems of equations. But for now, let's practice setting them up.

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
What is the coefficient matrix for the following system of linear equations?

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=1 \\ 2y &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, we organize the system so that every variable has a coefficient:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=1 \\ 0x+2y &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

$$
\left\lbrack
	\begin{matrix}
		1 & -2  \\
		0 & 2 
	\end{matrix}
	\right\rbrack
$$

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
What is the augmented matrix for the following system of linear equations?

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}y+x-5-3z &=0 \\ z &=y+7x \\ y+3-2z &=1-2x\end{aligned}\right.
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, we organize the system so that the variables are ordered $x,y,z$ on the left-hand side, the constants are on the right-hand side, and every variable has a coefficient:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y-3z &=5 \\ -7x-y+z &=0 \\ 2x+y-2z &=-2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

$$
\left\lbrack
	\begin{matrix}
		1 & 1 & -3  \\
		-7 & -1 & 1  \\
                2 & 1 & -2 
	\end{matrix}
	\right\rbrack
$$

The augmented matrix  is the coefficient matrix augmented with the column that represents the right-hand sides of the equations:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -3 & 5 \\ -7 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:

\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}5 & -4 & -12 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix consists of two parts: the coefficient matrix and the column of constants.

The coefficient matrix represents the coefficients in the linear system, while the column of constants represents the constants on the right-hand sides of the equations.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}5x-4y &=-12 \\ 3x+y &=1.\end{aligned}\right.

$$

$$

$$
\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

The augmented matrix is the coefficient matrix augmented with the column that represents the right-hand sides of the equations:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}-1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}-1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$
